lesson.title: Kubernetes from Zero, part 8: Services
lesson.description: Give Pods a stable name and IP with a Service. Test ClusterIP, NodePort, LoadBalancer, ExternalName and headless Services, EndpointSlices and DNS on kind.
lesson.tested: Every command ran on a kind v0.33.0 cluster (node v1.37.0, kubectl v1.37.2) on 10 Nov 2026
lesson.rule: Pods come and go; a Service gives them one stable name and IP, and its label selector decides which Pods get the traffic.

cheatsheet.intro: The five Service types, DNS, and the commands from Lesson 8.

boards.title: Five ways a Service answers
boards.hint: as the cheat sheet states them

rows.name: ClusterIP
rows.role: The default. Inside the cluster only. One stable virtual IP and DNS name.

rows.name: NodePort
rows.role: Opens the Service on every node. `nodePort` is in the range 30000-32767.

rows.name: LoadBalancer
rows.role: Asks the cloud for a load balancer. The external IP stays pending on kind.

rows.name: ExternalName
rows.role: A DNS alias to a name outside the cluster. CNAME only, no proxy.

items.what: A Service gives a changing set of Pods one stable virtual IP and DNS name. Its label selector picks the Pods.
EndpointSlices hold the current ready Pod IPs, and kube-proxy sends each connection to one of them.
Inside the namespace the short name `http://web` works. Across namespaces use `web.k8s-from-zero`. The full name ends in `.svc.cluster.local`.
Check endpoints first when a Service does not answer. A selector typo leaves Endpoints empty. A wrong target port lists Pod IPs that refuse the connection.

homework.intro: Use the kind cluster from part 3 and the namespace `k8s-from-zero` as your context namespace. The lesson's node is `k8s-ep07-control-plane`. The lab used kube-proxy in nftables mode, for the reason in When it goes wrong. Answers are in the separate answer key.

sections.title: Recall
sections.hint: Answer from memory, then check the lesson.

exercises.q: What does a Service give a set of Pods, and what picks the Pods?
exercises.a: One stable virtual IP and DNS name. Its label selector picks the Pods. On the lesson's kind cluster the Service range is `10.96.0.0/16`.

exercises.q: What do EndpointSlices hold, and who sends each connection?
exercises.a: The current ready Pod IPs. kube-proxy sends each connection to one of them. Only ready Pods are used.

exercises.q: Name the five Service forms in the cheat sheet and one fact about each.
exercises.a: ClusterIP is inside the cluster only. NodePort opens a port on every node, in 30000-32767. LoadBalancer asks a cloud for an address and stays pending on kind. ExternalName is a CNAME and does not proxy. A headless Service sets `clusterIP: None` so DNS returns Pod IPs.

exercises.q: Expose the Deployment and run `kubectl get svc -o wide`. Which extra column does `-o wide` add?
exercises.a: SELECTOR. Compare it with `kubectl get pods --show-labels` when a Service has no endpoints.

exercises.q: Run `kubectl get endpointslices -l kubernetes.io/service-name=web`. Which Pods are listed?
exercises.a: Ready Pods only. Pods that are not ready get no traffic.

exercises.q: From the client Pod, fetch `http://web` and `http://web.k8s-from-zero`. When does each name work?
exercises.a: `http://web` works in the same namespace. `http://web.k8s-from-zero` is the cross-namespace name. The full name adds `.svc.cluster.local`.

sections.title: Predict the outcome
sections.hint: Write your prediction first. Then check the answer key.

exercises.q: wget says connection refused and `kubectl describe service` shows an empty Endpoints line. What did the lesson cause this with?
exercises.a: A selector typo, `app.kubernetes.io/name: wbe`. Compare the SELECTOR column with the Pod labels and fix the selector.

exercises.q: Endpoints list Pod IPs, but connections are still refused. What did the lesson expose the Deployment with?
exercises.a: `--target-port=9999`. The slice showed `9999`, a port nothing listens on. Use a named port (`targetPort: http`) so the Service follows the container.

exercises.q: A LoadBalancer Service stays `EXTERNAL-IP` pending. What does the lesson say to use on kind?
exercises.a: NodePort or port-forward. Nothing in the cluster provisions load balancers. On a cloud cluster, check the cloud controller's events with `kubectl describe service`.
